env: > PostgreSQL 18.6 (Homebrew), Bun 1.4.2, Apple M4 Max, September 2026. Median µs per operation over 250 rounds, after 125 warmup rounds, interleaved and rotated. Every median is ±1.6% or tighter at 95% confidence (widest: Sequelize).
headline:
Totals only span 2.0x, because every entry pays the same database cost. What the ORM itself adds spans 8x: 176µs for UQL (bunSql), 1383µs for MikroORM.

Each entry is measured against its own driver's floor, so a faster driver is never counted as the ORM's win. Running the same UQL code on Bun SQL instead of `pg` saves 84µs, but only 51µs of that is UQL: the other 33µs is the gap between the two floors, free to anything on that driver.

memory-env: > PostgreSQL 18.6 (Homebrew), Node 24.20.0, Apple M4 Max, September 2026. Median KB allocated per step over 60 rounds after 60 warmup of a 7-step lifecycle. Rounds a garbage collection ran in are discarded, never corrected, and no entry lost more than 1% of its own (MikroORM).
memory-note:
Above the floor the field spans 17.3x: 209KB for UQL, 3621KB for MikroORM, and read opens it widest: MikroORM's 1470KB against UQL's 133KB.

Almost none of it survives: another 60 lifecycles, collected either side, leave every heap smaller than it started, identity maps included. What the table prices is collector pressure, not a resident set that grows.
runtime-env: > Bun 1.4.2, Node 24.20.0, Deno 2.9.6, all running the same bundled JavaScript, one at a time against the same database. PostgreSQL 18.6 (Homebrew), Apple M4 Max, September 2026. µs for a whole lifecycle, nearest-rank percentiles over 2000 rounds after 250 warmup, so a p99 is drawn from the 21 slowest rounds.
runtime-note: On `raw pg`, the same code on all of them, the runtimes are 72µs apart at p50 but 927µs apart at p99: Bun leads the median, Node the tail, and each p99 is 268% on Bun, 173% on Node, 174% on Deno above its own p50. Switching runtime moves any single entry by at most 1234µs at p50 (MikroORM), where switching ORM on one runtime moves it 1188-2426µs, so the runtime is the bigger decision here. The one pair that changes places between runtimes is Drizzle and TypeORM, 37µs apart.
